title: Potassium salts concentrate where cell-surface tension is weak

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Potassium salts concentrate where cell-surface tension is weak

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Potassium salts, like inorganic substances generally, raise surface tension and therefore concentrate at those parts of a cell surface where the tension is weak, so their localised accumulation (shown by Macallum's cobalt-nitrite method) indicates inequalities of surface tension.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VI: A Note on Adsorption

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: and we may safely take it that our potassium salts, like inorganic substances in general, tend to _raise_ the surface tension, and will therefore be found concentrating at a portion of the surface whose tension is weak

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VI, “A Note on Adsorption”; topic “Potassium concentration and weakened tension”. Scope: plant and animal cells, solitary and in tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch06-06: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.43

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claimed inverse spatial relation is testable, although 'weak tension' needs a modern mechanical definition. Available public imaging generally supplies either ion localization or mechanics, not both at sufficient resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map intracellular potassium concentration and local cortical tension in the same cells and test for inverse spatial association and predictable redistribution after tension perturbation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Historical cobalt-nitrite staining may not specifically report free potassium.

Public datasets rarely co-measure ion concentration and local tension.

discriminating power: 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim links two variables, potassium localization and local surface tension, by the physicochemical rule that these salts raise tension and therefore collect where tension is weak. Historical cobalt-nitrite plates and scattered elemental maps give the potassium side only. Without paired tension data the indicated mechanism cannot be confirmed or refuted from public datasets.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Co-register local potassium at the cell surface with an independent measure of local surface tension. Potassium enriched where tension is independently low, and inorganic salts shown to raise the relevant interfacial tension, would support the claim; potassium patterns that ignore measured tension, or tension inferred only from the potassium map, would not test it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Modern potassium imaging rarely shares a coordinate frame with a surface-tension measurement.

Using the potassium map itself as the tension map makes the test circular.
